This is a 1:15 scale model of the Titan IIIE rocket, developed by Martin Marietta for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). Using the U.S. Air Force Titan IIID as its basis, Titan IIIEs had liquid-fuel first and second stages, two strap-on solid rockets for extra boost at liftoff, and a liquid-fuel Centaur third stage.
NASA used the rocket from 1974 to 1977 to launch two Helios spacecraft to Mercury, two Viking spacecraft to Mars, and two Voyager spacecraft to the outer planets. Only one launch during this period failed. Martin Marietta made this model and donated it to NASM in 1983.

Built by [NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory](https://www.facebook.com/NASAJPL?__cft__[0]=AZhym5TzqtbV3Lwbp_E3hguEpYMOKcS9FInN4rr7PT0MDdIXSFEkP9E6mmiTsqfGTh1vfRkDOOXpT9N-WJ3McHYZq5OaJszRxHu9ohfwEkLcb7nXoAVpLbtKjAXAilbpnWem7V5yG_qjesb8dgQjW6HKnx2KiCl3&__tn__=-]K-R), the iconic, 722 kg spacecraft remains the only human-made object to visit all four giant planets of our solar system: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, returning breathtaking pictures of these distant worlds to Earth.
On November 5, 2018, Voyager 2 entered interstellar space at a distance of 17.9 billion km from the Sun. NASA remains in contact with the probe via the Deep Space Network.
Voyager 2 is one of only five human-made (all NASA) spacecraft to reach solar escape velocity, allowing them to leave the solar system. The probe travels at a speed of approx. 15.3 km/s.

## NASASpaceflight.com's Post
Built by [NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory](https://www.facebook.com/NASAJPL?__cft__[0]=AZhym5TzqtbV3Lwbp_E3hguEpYMOKcS9FInN4rr7PT0MDdIXSFEkP9E6mmiTsqfGTh1vfRkDOOXpT9N-WJ3McHYZq5OaJszRxHu9ohfwEkLcb7nXoAVpLbtKjAXAilbpnWem7V5yG_qjesb8dgQjW6HKnx2KiCl3&__tn__=-]K-R), the iconic, 722 kg spacecraft remains the only human-made object to visit all four giant planets of our solar system: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, returning breathtaking pictures of these distant worlds to Earth.
On November 5, 2018, Voyager 2 entered interstellar space at a distance of 17.9 billion km from the Sun. NASA remains in contact with the probe via the Deep Space Network.
Voyager 2 is one of only five human-made (all NASA) spacecraft to reach solar escape velocity, allowing them to leave the solar system. The probe travels at a speed of approx. 15.3 km/s.

This is a 1:15 scale model of the Titan IIIE rocket, developed by Martin Marietta for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). Using the U.S. Air Force Titan IIID as its basis, Titan IIIEs had liquid-fuel first and second stages, two strap-on solid rockets for extra boost at liftoff, and a liquid-fuel Centaur third stage.
NASA used the rocket from 1974 to 1977 to launch two Helios spacecraft to Mercury, two Viking spacecraft to Mars, and two Voyager spacecraft to the outer planets. Only one launch during this period failed. Martin Marietta made this model and donated it to NASM in 1983.

steps.text:
The first spacecraft to fly by Uranus was **Voyager 2**, which entered its Uranus encounter on 24 August 1986.  
Voyager 2 was launched on **a Titan III E‑Centaur launch vehicle** from Launch Complex‑41 at the Kennedy Space Center on 20 August 1977.
